info.title: Social Streamline API
info.description:
Publish to nine social platforms from your own code.

Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer ss_live_...`. Create a key in Settings, Developer.

Scopes are narrow on purpose: `posts:write` can draft but cannot send, and only `posts:publish` reaches an audience. Give an automated caller the smallest set that does its job.

apiKey.description: Scopes: posts:read, posts:write, posts:publish, accounts:read, accounts:write, media:read, media:write, analytics:read, jobs:read, jobs:write, ai:write, video:write, credits:read, presets:read, presets:write, webhooks:read, webhooks:write

post.description: Creates a draft. Nothing is sent anywhere until you call publish or schedule, which need the posts:publish scope. Media URLs must already be uploaded and publicly reachable. YouTube and TikTok take video only, and Instagram and Pinterest need an image or video: publishing or scheduling to them without that media is refused with platform_constraint.

post.description: Only short_video and long_video renders can be cancelled: cancelling releases a credit reservation, and the unbilled pipelines hold none. A render already in flight at the provider cannot be recalled, but nothing past the current step will run. The job is removed.

post.description:
Queues a landscape render from clips you have already uploaded. The facecam is composited over the desktop capture as picture-in-picture, unlike the short-form render which stacks them vertically. Spends credits, priced on total input duration measured server-side. Returns immediately; poll GET /jobs/{id}.

Spends credits or reaches an audience. Requires a key with this scope explicitly granted.

get.summary: Get performance totals and a per-platform breakdown
get.description: Aggregated over the last `days`. Counts only the most recent reading per post, since metrics accumulate over a post's life. Platforms are grouped, so one TikTok account connected through both APIs is one row. Metrics are collected on a schedule that starts about an hour after a post goes out, then slows as the post ages. A post published moments ago will not appear here yet: an empty summary right after publishing is expected, not a failure.
